 First Choice lead singer Rochelle Fleming dies at 72
 (November 7, 2026) We are sad to report to SoulTrackers the passing of Rochelle Fleming-Finney , the powerful lead singer of the legendary Philadelphia vocal group First Choice and one of the defining voices of the disco era. Her death was announced on her Facebook page by manager George Iz Correia, with the apt tribute, “She brought light, laughter and love to the world.”
 A Philadelphia native, the then Rochelle Fleming began singing with fellow Overbrook High School students, including Annette Guest and Wardell Piper, in a group originally known as The Debonettes. With help from legendary Philadelphia radio personality Georgie Woods, the young singers connected with producer Norman Harris and songwriter Allan Felder, changing the name to First Choice and beginning a partnership that established one of the important vocal groups of the Philly Soul movement.
 The group broke through nationally in 1973 with “Armed and Extremely Dangerous.” It went to #11 on the R&B chart and also reached the pop Top 30 and the UK Top 20. More success followed with “Smarty Pants,” “The Player” and “Guilty,” making the trio favorites among soul fans.
 But it was the group’s later work with Harris on the Gold Mind and Salsoul labels that cemented their place in dance music history. Songs such as “Doctor Love,” “Love Thang,” “Double Cross,” “Hold Your Horses” and the immortal “Let No Man Put Asunder” became club anthems. Fleming’s soaring, commanding vocals were the perfect match for those sophisticated Philadelphia arrangements and irresistible rhythms.
 After First Choice’s original breakup, Fleming continued as a solo artist, releasing dance recordings including “Love Itch,” “Danger!” and “Suffer the Consequences.” Meanwhile, her classic First Choice recordings kept finding new audiences through remixes, samples and covers.
 Fleming’s sad passing comes just a week after “Anywhere,” a nearly 50 year old song from her group mate, Wardell Piper , was released to critical acclaim , again reminding us of both the talent of the First Choice members, and the long term impact of their music.
 While she may not have been a household name, Rochelle Fleming’s voice echoed through our house growing up, and remains on repeat all these years later. May she rest in peace.
